title: Chinchilla Token Budget Is Empirical
subject: Machine Learning Theory
statement: Empirical compute-optimal scaling found that for a fixed compute budget many large language models were undertrained relative to their parameter count.
short: More tokens per parameter than earlier rules suggested.
long: More tokens per parameter than earlier rules suggested. The result comes from trained model families, not from a theorem.
proof: Empirical: isoFLOP comparisons show lower loss when parameters and tokens are scaled together.
consequence: Changed how training budgets are allocated.

title: Emergent Abilities May Be a Metric Artifact
subject: AI Systems & Evaluation
statement: Empirical analyses suggest that apparently abrupt emergence of capabilities can arise from smooth metrics such as accuracy or cross-entropy viewed on discontinuous scales.
short: Sharp emergence may be a scoring illusion.
long: Sharp emergence may be a scoring illusion. The debate concerns measurement, not whether capabilities improve.
proof: Empirical: replacing pass-or-fail metrics with continuous ones makes many jumps look gradual.
consequence: Calls for caution in claims about phase transitions.

title: In-Context Learning Resembles Bayesian Inference
subject: Natural Language Processing
statement: Empirical and theoretical work connects in-context learning to implicit Bayesian inference over tasks suggested by the prompt examples.
short: Prompts can act like evidence about the task.
long: Prompts can act like evidence about the task. Alternative accounts emphasize induction circuits and template matching.
proof: Constructed tasks show predictions consistent with posterior inference over latent concepts.
consequence: Provides a conceptual framework for prompting.

title: Few-Shot Label Distribution Biases Predictions Empirically
subject: Natural Language Processing
statement: Empirically, the distribution of labels in few-shot demonstrations biases the model's predicted label distribution.
long: Demonstration labels skew the answers. Balanced demonstration sets reduce the skew.
proof: Empirical: varying demo label frequencies shifts prediction frequencies on the same queries.

title: Chain-of-Thought Emerges with Scale Empirically
subject: Natural Language Processing
statement: Empirically, prompting for intermediate reasoning steps improves performance mainly for sufficiently large models.
short: Step-by-step prompting pays off at scale.
long: Step-by-step prompting pays off at scale. Small models can even be hurt by such prompts.
proof: Empirical: scaling studies compare direct and chain-of-thought prompts across model sizes.
consequence: Links reasoning behavior to model scale.

title: Self-Consistency Averages Reasoning Paths
subject: Natural Language Processing
statement: Self-consistency samples multiple reasoning chains and selects the most frequent final answer instead of relying on a single chain.
long: Vote across many reasoning paths. It trades inference cost for reliability.
proof: Sampling diverse chains lets consistent answers accumulate support across independent derivations.

title: Least-to-Most Prompting Decomposes Problems
subject: Natural Language Processing
statement: Least-to-most prompting first decomposes a problem into subproblems and then solves them in order, using earlier answers as context.
short: Break a hard problem into easier steps.
long: Break a hard problem into easier steps. It helps on compositional tasks such as multi-hop reasoning.
proof: Solving simpler subquestions first supplies intermediate results needed for later steps.
consequence: A structured alternative to single-pass reasoning.

title: Tree of Thoughts Explores Reasoning Branches
subject: Natural Language Processing
statement: Tree-of-thought prompting maintains several partial reasoning paths, evaluates them and expands the most promising ones.
long: Search over several reasoning branches. It borrows from search algorithms rather than following one chain.
proof: Generating and scoring candidate continuations lets the system prune weak paths.
consequence: Improves planning on tasks with multiple solution routes.

title: Instruction Tuning Improves Zero-Shot Behavior Empirically
subject: Natural Language Processing
statement: Empirically, fine-tuning language models on diverse instruction-response pairs improves their zero-shot performance on unseen tasks.
short: Training on instructions helps on new instructions.
long: Training on instructions helps on new instructions. Data diversity matters more than sheer volume in many studies.
proof: Empirical: instruction-tuned models outperform their base versions on held-out task formats.
consequence: A standard step in building general-purpose assistants.
